headline: Rainforest Trust Hits 70 Million Acres Protected
meta_description: Conservation organization reaches historic milestone protecting 70 million acres worldwide, adding 10 million acres in just 8 months with help from local partn…
summary_short: Rainforest Trust and local partners have protected over 70 million acres globally—an area the size of Nevada—with a dramatic push adding 10 million acres in eight months.
body:
Rainforest Trust and its local partners have crossed a historic threshold: protecting more than 70 million acres of land worldwide, an area equivalent to the entire state of Nevada.

The milestone reflects a dramatic acceleration in conservation work. The organization added 10 million of those protected acres in just eight months, demonstrating how coordinated effort between international groups and on-the-ground partners can scale impact rapidly. The milestone was reached through work in Bolivia, underscoring the importance of protecting rainforests across Latin America's critical ecosystems.

The achievement highlights a growing model of conservation: rather than relying solely on distant organizations, Rainforest Trust works alongside local communities and partners who understand their landscapes deeply. That combination of resources, expertise, and commitment to place is proving effective at preserving some of Earth's most biodiverse and carbon-rich environments at meaningful scale.
